play_campaign_owner_status(campaign_id).map_err(|_| PlayError::BadRequest)?;\n    if owner != actor {\n        return Err(PlayError::Conflict);\n    }\n    let (current_actor, phase, turn_number) =\n        play_campaign_get_turn(campaign_id).map_err(|_| PlayError::BadRequest)?;\n    if current_actor != \"dm\" || (phase != \"dm\" && phase != \"exploration\") {\n        return escape_json(&next_actor),\n        new_turn_number\n    ))\n}\n\n/// Parse a play campaign scene sub-resource path.\n///\n/// For example, `/v1/play/campaigns/{id}/scenes/{scene_id}/enter` Defaults to `game.db` in the working\n/// directory.\npub fn db_path() -> String {\n    env::var(\"DB_PATH\").unwrap_or_else(|_| \"game.db\".to_string())\n}\n\n/// Escape a single quote for safe concatenation into SQLite string literals.\n///\n/// This application builds SQL by string concatenation rather than using\n/// parameterized queries, so every user-supplied string must be escaped before\n/// being embedded in a SQL statement.\npub fn sql_escape(s: &str) -> String {\n    s.replace('\\'', \"''\")\n}\n\n/// Execute a SQL script against the SQLite database without capturing output.\n///\n/// Returns an error if `sqlite3` cannot be spawned or exits with a non-zero\n/// status.\npub fn sqlite_exec(sql: &str) -> Result<(), String> {\n    let mut child = Command::new(\"sqlite3\")\n        .arg(db_path())\n        .arg(\"-bail\")\n        .stdin(Stdio::piped())\n        .stdout(Stdio::piped())\n        .stderr(Stdio::piped())\n        .spawn()\n        .map_err(|e| format!(\"sqlite3 spawn failed: {}\", e))?;\n\n    if let Some(mut stdin) = child.stdin.take() {\n        stdin\n            .write_all(sql.as_bytes())\n            .map_err(|e| format!(\"sqlite3 stdin write: {}\", e))?;\n    }\n\n    let output = child\n        .wait_with_output()\n        .map_err(|e| format!(\"sqlite3 output: {}\", e))?;\n    if !output.status.success() {\n        return Err(format!(\n            \"sqlite3 error: {}\",\n            String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)\n        ));\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Execute a SQL query and return the SQLite JSON-mode result as a string.\n///\n/// The output is produced with `.mode json`, so well-formed results are a JSON\n/// array of objects. Empty results are returned as an empty string.\npub fn sqlite_query(sql: &str) -> Result<String, String> {\n    let input = format!(\".mode json\\n{}\\n\", sql);\n    let mut child = Command::new(\"sqlite3\")\n        .arg(db_path())\n        .stdin(Stdio::piped())\n        .stdout(Stdio::piped())\n        .stderr(Stdio::piped())\n        .spawn()\n        .map_err(|e| format!(\"sqlite3 spawn failed: {}\", e))?;\n\n    if let Some(mut stdin) = child.stdin.take() {\n        stdin\n            .write_all(input.as_bytes())\n            .map_err(|e| format!(\"sqlite3 stdin write: {}\", e))?;\n    }\n\n    let output = child\n        .wait_with_output()\n        .map_err(|e| format!(\"sqlite3 output: {}\", e))?;\n    if !output.status.success() {\n        return Err(format!(\n            \"sqlite3 error: {}\",\n            String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)\n        ));\n    }\n    Ok(String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).trim().to_string())\n}\n\n/// column to a table if it does not already exist.\n///\n/// `definition` must include the full column clause, e.g.\n/// `\"status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'healthy'\"`. This is used by the startup\n/// migrations to make older schemas forward-compatible without altering\n/// behavior for newly created databases.\nfn add_column_if_missing(table: &str, column: &str, definition: &str) -> Result<(), String> {\n    let sql = format!(\"PRAGMA table_info({});\", table);\n    let output = sqlite_query(&sql)?;\n\n    let content = extract_top_array_content(&output).unwrap_or(\"\");\n    let has_column = extract_objects(content)\n        .into_iter()\n        .filter_map(|o| extract_string(o, \"name\"))\n        .any(|name| name == column);\n    if !has_column {\n        sqlite_exec(&format!(\"ALTER TABLE {} ADD COLUMN {};\", table, definition))?;\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Add missing death-save columns to an existing play_campaign_members table.\n///\n/// Older schemas created before the death-saves stage lack `status`,\n/// `death_saves_successes`, and `death_saves_failures`. This is used by the startup\n/// migrations to make older schemas forward-compatible without altering\n/// behavior for newly created databases.\nfn add_column_if_missing(table: &str, column: &str, definition: &str) -> Result<(), String> {\n    let sql = format!(\"PRAGMA table_info({});\", table);\n    let output = sqlite_query(&sql)?;\n\n    let content = extract_top_array_content(&output).unwrap_or(\"\");\n    let has_column = extract_objects(content)\n        .into_iter()\n        .filter_map(|o| extract_string(o, \"name\"))\n        .any(|name| name == column);\n    if !has_column {\n        sqlite_exec(&format!(\"ALTER TABLE {} ADD COLUMN {};\", table, definition))?;\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Add missing death-save columns to an existing play_campaign_members table.\n///\n/// Older schemas created before the death-saves stage lack `status`,\n/// `death_saves_successes`, and `death_saves_failures`. to_gold_after = to_gold_before + gold;\n\n    let sql = format!(\n        \"BEGIN;\\nUPDATE play_campaign_members SET gold = {} WHERE campaign_id = '{}' AND character_id = '{}';\\nUPDATE play_campaign_members SET gold = {} WHERE campaign_id = '{}' AND character_id = '{}';\\nINSERT INTO play_currency_transfers (campaign_id, transfer_id, from_character_id, to_character_id, gold) VALUES ('{}', {}, '{}', '{}', {});\\nCOMMIT;\",\n        from_gold_after,\n        sql_escape(campaign_id),\n        sql_escape(from_character_id),\n        to_gold_after,\n        sql_escape(campaign_id),\n        sql_escape(to_character_id),\n        sql_escape(campaign_id),\n        transfer_id,\n        sql_escape(from_character_id),\n        sql_escape(to_character_id),\n        gold\n    );\n    sqlite_exec(&sql)?;\n    Ok((transfer_id, from_gold_after, to_gold_after))\n}\n\n/// Return the actor, owner, class, level, and hp_max for a play campaign member by character id.\n///\n/// This tuple The request body must\n/// contain a `level` exactly one higher than the current level. Maximum hit\n/// points increase by the deterministic class hit die average plus the\n/// constitution modifier derived from the level-1 build.\npub fn level_up_character(\n    campaign_id: &str,\n    character_id: &str,\n    body: &str,\n    actor: &str,\n) -> Result<String, PlayError> {\n    if !play_campaign_exists(campaign_id).map_err(|_| PlayError::BadRequest)? {\n        return
